Resolution Summary: RCS-26519 Date: 2026-06-29

Issue reported: After Platform Unification, TBI ApprissCase users were not receiving their Secure Incident security level via SSO/SSO+. Users could not log in to Secure Incident, or could not see records across all locations, blocking the planned 3,000+ user Incident rollout.

Root cause: The new sso.SecurityLevelAssignments table (Platform Unification, assigns Secure Incident roles via SSO+) was not replicating into Secure. The replication path was incomplete (table/load plus YADL mapping), compounded by a Snowflake configuration / duplicate-table issue that selected the wrong source, plus a fix PR merged to main that was overwritten by a release deploy. SSO users authenticated but their Incident security level never landed in Secure (empty Incident Security ID).

Resolution: Delivered under RCS-27269. New table ardm_209.sso_securitylevelassignments derives the security level from the existing teams file (tlog_209.appriss_sso_teams) and replicates to sso.securitylevelassignments. PR: https://dev.azure.com/apprissdevops/DataOps/_git/c209tbi/pullrequest/53501 (plus arpfiles YADL Mappings.json update and Carl Costelow's Snowflake config correction). Replication across the SSO tables confirmed current; production confirmed fixed (Matthew Kamminga). Ingesting the SSO files now assigns users their locations, permission groups/teams, and incident roles automatically. Customer updated by Shelley Cameron on RCS-27269 (2026-06-24). Closing RCS-26519 as resolved by RCS-27269. Caveat: existing manual SSO+ entries can override file-feed assignments (TBI deciding whether to have these removed, tracked on RCS-27269). Related: RCS-27578 (new-user recurrence, with M. Kamminga), RCS-27325.

Hello Colton,

We are pleased to confirm that the Secure Incident permissions issue has now been resolved.

The SSO files you send are now ingested in full, so each user is automatically assigned their location hierarchy, their permission groups and teams, and their Secure Incident role when they log in. The Incident security level no longer needs to be applied manually for new or existing users going forward, which supports your wider Incident rollout.

We will go ahead and mark this ticket as completed. The fix is already live, so please feel free to have your users continue logging in and using Secure Incident as normal. You are welcome to reply here if anything comes up as your team works through it, and we will be happy to help. Otherwise the ticket will close automatically within one week.

Kind regards, Matthew Everett Appriss Retail Support

  1. Location hierarchy access — users need to be assigned to at least one store/location. If their hierarchy shows "the whole company" that should be fine, but worth confirming it's actually applied.

  2. SSO+ profile sync — if Tailored Brands uses SSO, the permissions in the SSO master file may not match what's shown in the user profile. The SSO+ section in Settings should match the Users section.

Unfortunately I don’t believe any other users that are listed as “Corporate User” for Secure Incident and also have ApprissCase Search User listed.

Hello Colton,

Thank you for your patience on this. I've identified and resolved the issue.

The user profile and Incident location were both correctly showing KNG 0308, as you confirmed. However, there is a separate identity layer tied to the SSO login process (SSO+ Location Hierarchy) that controls what store a user actually sees when they sign in. For Tracy, this layer was empty — it didn't have any store location assigned, which caused the system to fall back to her old store assignment (KNG 0030).

I've added KNG 0308 (Lewisville) to Tracy's SSO+ Location Hierarchy. Could you please have Tracy do the following:

  2. Close the browser

  3. Log back in and try creating an incident report

Delivery Team Escalation — RCS-27325 | Tailored Brands — SSO+ Location Hierarchy Not Updating on Store Transfers

Client: Tailored Brands
Environment: apps.apprissretail.com/tailoredbrands/platform/
Filed by: Colton Neal (colton.neal@tailoredbrands.com)

What's happening:
When a Tailored Brands user transfers stores, their SSO+ Location Hierarchy is not being updated by the daily feed. The main profile Hierarchies tab and the Incident store record both update correctly — but the SSO+ layer remains on the old store, causing the user to see their previous location when they log in.

Confirmed affected users:

  • Tracy Lamoureux — transferred KNG 0030 → KNG 0308 (April 2026). SSO+ Location Hierarchy was empty. Manually added KNG 0308 as a workaround.

  • Patrick Caughron — transferred KNG 0308 → KNG 0030. Same pattern — SSO+ Location Hierarchy not reflecting current store.

What the client expects:
Colton confirmed that Tailored Brands sends a daily feed that should automatically populate permissions, teams, and location hierarchy. SSO+ should not require manual intervention for routine transfers. They are treating SSO+ as an emergency/backup tool only.

What we need from Delivery:

  1. Confirm whether the daily feed is configured to update SSO+ Location Hierarchy on store transfers, or if this mapping is missing/broken

  2. Identify how many other Tailored Brands users may be in the same state (transferred but SSO+ not updated)

  3. Recommend a fix so transfers propagate automatically going forward

Workaround applied: SSO+ Location Hierarchy manually updated for Tracy Lamoureux. Patrick Caughron still needs the same manual fix pending Delivery's review.

INTERNAL NOTE

@Simon Smith — Passing along some additional context that may help move this forward.

Scope Update:
Colton just reported 3 more affected users at KNG 0030 — Malcolm Patrick, Teegan Baker, and Kalee Delong. All attempted to access Appriss Incident today and could not see their assigned store. That brings the confirmed affected count to 5+ (Tracy Lamoureux, Patrick Caughron, Malcolm Patrick, Teegan Baker, Kalee Delong). This is not a per-user issue — it's systemic.

Ryan Barlow's Finding:
Ryan flagged the data load log to you earlier today and it tells the story. The daily SSO+ feed runs and successfully loads:

  • [sso].[Teams] — 4,058 rows inserted ✅

  • [sso].[PermissionGroups] — 4,186 rows inserted ✅

  • [sso].[LocationHierarchyMembers] — 0 rows from source ❌

The log line reads: External source search over source table "sso.LocationHierarchyMembers" on connection "securereferencedata-direct" returned no rows.

The feed is running. Teams and PermissionGroups populate fine. But the source query for LocationHierarchyMembers returns nothing — that's why every transferred user's SSO+ Location Hierarchy is empty.

What Needs To Happen:
The source connection "securereferencedata-direct" for the LocationHierarchyMembers table needs to be traced — what is it pointing at, is the source table/view populated, and was this mapping ever configured correctly for Tailored Brands? Ryan Barlow has deep knowledge of the Incident-side architecture and may be able to help trace where that source connection resolves to if you need a second pair of eyes on it.

Duplicate Store Number Flag:
Colton also flagged that TB reuses store numbers across brands (KNG0030 and MSP0030). Worth checking whether the LocationHierarchyMembers source logic disambiguates by brand prefix or just store number — if it's store number only, that could cause collisions.

Client Expectation:
Colton has been clear that the daily feed should handle this automatically. They treat SSO+ manual edits as emergency-only. Until the feed source is fixed, every store transfer will require manual intervention.

Hello,

I spoke with the users at this store location, and they are able to successfully login and view their correct store.

Colton Neal
